b1.summary: Every run fixed the vert.x HTTP permission path and the injected static-exclusion rule, then missed the Undertow servlet-constraint matcher (%3B / %00 spellings, 6/6 runs). Four runs (all MiMo, DeepSeek run 1) canonicalised in a way that lets /api/secure/..;/open/data escape the routed admin rule. That failure sits in the functional group but is itself an access-control loosening, and it zeroes the reward through the threshold rule.

b2.note: The %00 servlet case fails in all 6 runs and is the only failure of DeepSeek run 2 (0.9091). The other runs fail 3 or more tests.

b4.note: MiMo's three runs are identical (servlet plus loosening). DeepSeek varies: full miss plus loosening, %00 only, or all three servlet spellings.

b5.open_human_question: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES, but not on decisive tests: confirm the exact 404 on the ordinary excluded static path and that the injected excluded-paths rule falls under 'every protection ... based on a request path'. Three 'Required: generalize' rewrites (static content wording, the path-parameter sentence, 'encoded separator' in the public clause) are not applied to instruction.md.

b6.reason: The servlet trap is covered: upstream 919b800 switches ServletHttpSecurityPolicy to HttpSecurityUtils.normalizePath (full decode, matrix strip, \0 removal) and adds %3B servlet tests. The loosening trap is uncovered. Upstream's own decode-plus-removeDots, which never checks the routed path, is exactly the functional_fail_over_normalization wrong fix, so copying upstream fails it. DeepSeek runs 2 and 3 are decided only by the covered servlet trap.

quotes: no normalisation may turn a request that is refused today into one that is allowed: whatever resource a request actually reaches must still be covered by the decision that covers its canonical location
This holds for every protection the product applies based on a request path, and for every mechanism that serves the resource.
it is not the full set of affected paths, spellings or rules
b7.note: The first quote states the loosening trap's rule almost directly. Servlets are never named.

b8.gate: .sound (nop 11/11 sec fail; oracle 3x 1.0; 5 patch checks as declared)
b8.note: pass_alternative.patch (a different RequestPaths canonicaliser) and pass_hardening.patch pass.

c1.mechanism: authorization bypass by path normalisation (encoded separator, encoded matrix ';', null byte): the authz decision and the resource resolution read different paths

c2.pattern: missed second copy (second authz implementation) + over-normalised into a weaker rule
c2.note: Servlet: a real second implementation in another extension that upstream also fixes. Loosening: the natural canonicalisation, which is upstream's own fix, opens a routed protected path. The injected static-exclusion sibling was solved by all 6 runs.

d2.evidence: The injection adds a StaticPathRules class, a documented static-resources excludedPaths() config key and two guard calls in StaticResourcesRecorder. It is idiomatic Quarkus code with standard Javadoc and makes the same normalizedPath()-vs-decoded slip as the real bug. The comment 'excluded paths must never be served as static content' is neutral. It was not decisive: every run fixed it.

e2.why: All 6 runs are trusted, all at medium confidence, none high.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open (on a non-decisive test), and the required generalisations were not applied.

e4.why: The servlet subtree is served to anonymous callers in every run.

e5.why: Partly: the servlet trap is covered by upstream 919b800 and alone decides DeepSeek runs 2 and 3. Only the loosening trap (MiMo, DeepSeek run 1) survives a lookup.

concerns: The upstream fix covers the servlet trap, so a model that looks it up could clear DeepSeek runs 2 and 3.
MiMo's 0.0 rewards come from a functional-group test through the threshold rule, although that test checks a real access-control loosening.
The %00 case alone decides DeepSeek run 2 (0.9091).
The open human-review flag and the unapplied required generalisations (instruction hints).
The injected sibling contributed nothing decisive.
All audits are medium confidence: no final code or transcript.
one_line: Quarkus path authz: models canonicalise the HTTP permission path but miss the servlet-constraint copy, and MiMo's canonicalisation lets a ..;-path escape a routed admin rule, the same mistake upstream's fix makes.
